look_here_first: LOOK AT THE STEM FIRST: broad, wavy leaflike WINGS run vertically DOWN from the leaf base along the green stem. Follow a leaf to its decurrent ridges with your finger. Then check ALTERNATE rough toothed leaves and a broad autumn canopy of MANY TINY white composite heads (usually only 1–3 white rays per head). Winter ICE RIBBONS at split bases are memorable but seasonal—not required for ID.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Tall herbaceous perennial, often 1–2.2 m in regional Williamson County specimens, robust 1–several unbranched lower stems beneath a much-branched terminal flowering canopy.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Usually alternate (lower-most sometimes opposite), simple, rough-hairy / scabrous, often elliptic to ovate or lance-elliptic, with long tapering sessile/petiolar bases extending down the stem as wings; edges often coarsely toothed but can be almost entire. Larger mid-stem leaves and variable sizes—do not key entirely on individual leaf outline.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Terminal branched flat to domed clusters with dozens of very small white radiate composite heads, often 60–100+ heads. Each head usually only (0–)1–3(–5) short white ray florets around about 8–13 off-white to cream disc florets in regional populations. NOT a big daisy-like head.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: Outer narrow green bracts in 1–2 series beneath each tiny head; UT Williamson describes ca. 5 main outer phyllaries, ~2–2.5 mm long. Receptacular paleae wrap the disc florets, so examine with a hand lens if separating close relatives.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Winged flattened cypselae (achenes), ca. 4–6 mm in Williamson populations, with TWO straight persistent bristlelike pappus AWNS ~1.5–3 mm; not 'pappus reduced or absent'. Papery lateral fruit wings are distinct from stem wings.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: alternately attached rough leaves with tapering/decurrent bases

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: tall perennial with many white very-small heads in flat/panicled canopy

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: each white head typically just 1–3 little ray florets (not a large daisy)

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: ice ribbons around split old lower stems after first hard freezes (seasonal bonus)

key_traits.label: Stems
key_traits.text: Thick pale-to-deep green lower stem frequently with conspicuous vertical WINGS decurrent from leaf bases. UT Williamson: wavy thin wings ca. 3–5.5 mm wide; stems short-hirsute with a white solid pith. Wings can become reduced/lost on aging woody basal portions; inspect intact green internodes.

key_traits.label: Rays vs disc
key_traits.text: Ray FLORETS: few, each white and strap-shaped, pistillate. DISC FLORETS: several small tubular florets, bisexual, cream/white. A 'flower head' is a capitulum containing multiple individual florets.

key_traits.label: Frost flower
key_traits.text: During some early freezes, water supplied from still-active roots emerges through cracks in dying lower stem and freezes into delicate ice ribbons; duration is short and occurrence is weather-dependent. Not all plants or freezing mornings show this.
